title: Numbers 0–100
summary: Count to a hundred, and make numbers agree: un libro, veintiuna chicas, cien euros.
focus: Cardinal numbers 0–100 and their agreement with nouns
content:
## 0 to 15: learn these as words

cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez, once, doce, trece, catorce, quince.

## 16 to 29: one word

From 16 to 29 the numbers are written as one word: **dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve, veinte, veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés, veinticuatro, veinticinco, veintiséis, veintisiete, veintiocho, veintinueve**. Note the accents on *dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis*.

## 30 to 99: tens + y + units

The tens are **treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta, sesenta, setenta, ochenta, noventa**. Join the units with **y**: *treinta y uno, cuarenta y cinco, noventa y nueve*.

## 100

Use **cien** on its own or directly before a noun: *cien euros, cien personas*. Above 100 it becomes *ciento*: *ciento diez*.

## Numbers with nouns

**Uno** changes before a noun: **un** before a masculine noun, **una** before a feminine one.

- *un libro, una mesa, veintiún años, veintiuna chicas, treinta y una personas*

All other numbers are invariable: *dos casas, cuarenta coches*.

Numbers themselves are masculine: *el dos, el quince*. Ages use **tener**: *Tengo veintidós años.* Prices use **ser** or **costar**: *Son diez euros.*

quiz.explanation: 16–29 are one word; veintidós carries an accent.
Tens and units are joined with y.
Before a masculine noun uno shortens to un: veintiún años.
Exactly one hundred before a noun is cien.
Uno becomes una before a feminine noun: treinta y una chicas.

hints: Tens end in -enta (except veinte and treinta).

quiz.explanation: Age is expressed with tener: tiene cincuenta años.

listening.text: Dos cafés con leche, por favor.

listening.meaning: My brother is twenty-three years old.

listening.text: Mi abuela tiene ochenta y cuatro años.
listening.meaning: My grandmother is eighty-four years old.

listening.text: El libro cuesta veinticinco euros en la tienda.
listening.meaning: The book costs twenty-five euros in the shop.
listening.note: New word: la tienda = the shop.

listening.text: Vivimos en el número cincuenta y seis.
listening.note: New word: el número = the number.

listening.text: ¿Cuántos años tiene tu madre? Tiene sesenta y un años.
listening.meaning: How old is your mother? She is sixty-one.
listening.note: Uno becomes un before a masculine noun: sesenta y un años.

listening.text: Mi abuelo tiene noventa y nueve años y vive solo en Madrid.
listening.meaning: My grandfather is ninety-nine years old and lives alone in Madrid.

conversations.title: At the market
conversations.scenario: Carmen buys fruit from a market seller and asks the price.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Good morning. How much are the oranges?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Dos euros el kilo. Las manzanas, uno cincuenta.
lines.meaning: Two euros a kilo. The apples, one fifty.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Quiero tres kilos de naranjas y un kilo de manzanas.
lines.meaning: I want three kilos of oranges and one kilo of apples.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y dos cincuenta de cambio. ¿Cuántos años tiene su hija?
lines.meaning: And two fifty change. How old is your daughter?

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: She's fifteen. She eats lots of oranges!

bites.title: 16 to 29: squash it
bites.rule: Up to 29, the number is one word: dieciséis, veintidós. Watch the accents on -séis, -dós and -trés.

bites.title: From 30: tens y units
bites.rule: From 30 on, glue tens and units with y: treinta y uno, cuarenta y cinco. The y only goes between tens and units.

bites.title: Uno shape-shifts
bites.rule: Before a noun, uno turns into un (masculine) or una (feminine), even at the end of a big number: veintiún años, treinta y una personas.
bites.example: un libro, una mesa, veintiún años
bites.example_meaning: one book, one table, twenty-one years

bites.title: Cien is a clean hundred
bites.rule: Exactly 100, or 100 right before a noun, is cien. It becomes ciento only when more number follows.
bites.example_meaning: a hundred euros, a hundred and ten

sorts.title: One word or three?
sorts.why: 16 to 29 are written as one word; from 31 on it's tens + y + units.

sorts.title: Un, una or uno?
sorts.why: Before a masculine noun it's un, before a feminine one una; on its own it stays uno.

sorts.title: Cien or ciento?
sorts.why: Cien is used alone or right before a noun; ciento is followed by more number.

spots.why: Before a masculine noun, -uno shortens: veintiún años.
Chicas is feminine, so the number ends in una.
Exactly 100 before a noun is cien.

spots.sentence: Hay uno libro en la mesa.
spots.why: Uno shortens to un before a masculine noun.
Dieciséis carries an accent on the last syllable.
Chicas is feminine, so it's veintiuna.
